clue.text: Arrange again a holiday spot offering rest or variety

indicators.note: variety implies a change of form, so the words rest and or are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A place to holiday is rearranged so it offers rest or something different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange again' is a further cryptic hint at the answer read as RE-SORT; the wordplay proper is 'variety' shuffling REST and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town or spa where people go on vacation is called a resort.

clue.text: Loosen up about lacking firmness

parts.note: re means about or concerning
lax means slack or not strict

explanation.surface: Unwind concerning being slack.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to ease tension and stop being tense.

clue.text: Narrow channels represent a very difficult situation

definitions.meaning: narrow sea passages between two land masses

explanation.definitionFit: Sea passages such as Gibraltar's are called this, and being in dire trouble is being in this.

clue.text: Highly regarded editor pursues detail

indicators.note: pursues means the editor follows on after the other piece

parts.note: a respect is a particular point or detail, as in every respect

explanation.surface: An esteemed editor chases a fine point.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone admired and well thought of is held in esteem.

clue.text: A high regard for bridge players, team heard

parts.note: East and South, two of the four seats at a bridge table, abbreviated E and S

indicators.note: heard tells us the word team is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the word team, said aloud, matches a word meaning to pour or swarm

explanation.surface: Respect shown to a group of bridge players, as the team are told.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so E and S are a pair of them; TEAM spoken sounds like TEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Great respect or admiration is a synonym for holding someone in high regard.

clue.text: Plump for strong drink

definitions.meaning: a dark, strong beer such as porter

explanation.definitionFit: A portly build is called this, and so is a dark heavy beer like Guinness.

clue.text: Sty case to be doctored with drug

indicators.note: something doctored is tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pigsty case is to be treated with medication.
explanation.definitionFit: A recreational stimulant also known as MDMA goes by this name.

clue.text: Spoil mum — lead off with what's been preserved for breakfast

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
ma is an informal name for one's mother

indicators.note: off means the word lead goes wrong and is rearranged

explanation.surface: Ruin Mum's lead, ending up with a breakfast preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus jam, typically orange, eaten on toast in the morning is this preserve.

clue.text: Play sorrowfully without opening the sherry

indicators.note: without opening tells us to drop the first letter of the musical term

parts.note: doloroso is the Italian musical direction telling a performer to play in a sorrowful manner

explanation.surface: A musician plays sadly, having failed to open the bottle of sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: DOLOROSO is a musical direction (Italian for sorrowful); 'without opening' removes its first letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, rich style of Spanish sherry from Jerez.

clue.text: Agree with companion

definitions.meaning: to keep company or go along with them
a spouse or partner, especially of a monarch

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means keep company or be in harmony; as a noun it means a partner, like a royal spouse.

clue.text: Decide to put a stop to tunnel

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or prevent
a mine is an underground tunnel

explanation.surface: Make up one's mind to halt the digging.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle or resolve something is to fix it firmly.

clue.text: Old cement protects it from kicks

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife

indicators.note: protects suggests one word wrapped around another to shield it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ancient mortar shields something from being kicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicks' is a noun here, as in doing something for kicks, meaning for thrills; 'Old' looks like it describes the cement but supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrills sought for fun are called kicks, as in doing something just for the buzz.

clue.text: Amateur means to be elsewhere

parts.note: a way is a means or method of doing something

explanation.surface: Being a non-professional means you are somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: Being absent, not present here, is the same as being somewhere other than this place.

clue.text: Start with working group

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a set is a group of things that belong together

explanation.surface: Begin with a team that is up and running.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something, like an illness, is its onset.

clue.text: Not even the cricketer dismissed one excluded from the group

parts.note: odd numbers are those that are not even
a man is a player, such as a cricketer
a batter who is dismissed is out

explanation.surface: Uneven: the cricketer was given out, leaving him excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter who is dismissed is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who does not fit in or is left over when others pair up.

clue.text: Ordinary night before railway day

parts.note: an eve is the evening or night before a special day, like Christmas Eve
taken as written

explanation.surface: A normal evening ahead of a day spent on the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Commonplace, routine things are described as being run-of-the-mill or day-to-day.

clue.text: Able somehow to make speech complicated

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unknown way of arranging things, so Able's letters are mixed

parts.note: to orate is to deliver a speech

explanation.surface: Able somehow to give a speech that is intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate and detailed things are complex.

clue.text: Madden dumbfounded readers by including something extra

indicators.note: including signals that the run of letters is contained within the words Madden dumbfounded

explanation.surface: Readers were astonished that a football figure called Madden had added an appendix.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'mADDEN DUMbfounded', which the clue's readers are said to include.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition at the end of a book or document is a supplementary section.

clue.text: Lift me up on bolster for a cuddle

indicators.note: up on means the first piece sits above the second in this down entry
in a down clue lifting a word turns it upside down, so me is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to brace is to support or bolster

explanation.surface: Raise me up on a pillow for a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'Lift' turns the word upwards, and 'up on' places it above the support.
explanation.definitionFit: A hug or holding someone in one's arms is an affectionate squeeze.

clue.text: A classical European unfinished accord

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is removed from the word for the European

parts.note: a Greek is a European, and ancient Greece is the classical world

explanation.surface: An old-world European fails to finish signing an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord is to concur or be in harmony, a verb sense matching to concur.

clue.text: Stood up, having fed, looking pink

parts.note: rose means got up to stand
ate means having eaten food

explanation.surface: Getting up after a meal, someone looks flushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosy-coloured, the hue of a flower, is a poetic word for pink.

clue.text: An innocent child called Elia

definitions.meaning: a gentle, guileless young person is often called a little ...
Elia was the pen name of the English essayist Charles ...

explanation.definitionFit: An innocent youngster is a lamb in metaphor, and the essayist who wrote as Elia was Charles Lamb.

clue.text: VDU features poorly on shelf below glass pane

parts.note: a computer screen (visual display unit) shows windows
poorly means unwell or sick

explanation.surface: A computer monitor is working badly while sitting on a ledge.
explanation.walkthrough: VDU (visual display unit) is a British term for a computer monitor, whose screen shows windows.
explanation.definitionFit: The ledge at the base of a window frame, beneath the glass, is a sill.

clue.text: Very strange one pulled up outside

indicators.note: outside means the turned word goes around the letter for one
in a down clue up means the word for pulled is read from bottom to top

parts.note: drew means pulled, as a cart is drawn
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A very odd person is hauled up outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DREW into WERD, and 'outside' puts that around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre or uncanny things are odd in the extreme.

clue.text: The French have not started to go away

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: not started means the word have loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The French have yet to begin to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart or exit is to quit a place.

clue.text: Stay together, taking care of practice

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of
a habit is a regular practice

explanation.surface: Remaining a couple involves looking after one's routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who live under one roof without marrying are said to live together.

clue.text: Crackers with fruit and nuts

definitions.meaning: yellow tropical fruit grown in bunches
nuts is also slang for mad

explanation.definitionFit: The slang for mad matches both crackers and nuts, and the plural names a yellow fruit.

clue.text: Thick woollen suits tai-lered in West End, not North

indicators.note: tailored suggests cutting and reshaping, so the letters are rearranged
not tells us to leave out the letter for North

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: Heavy wool suits are tailored in London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N (North) from WEST END to leave WESTED, then 'tai-lered' (tailored) rearranges those six letters. The West End is London's central shopping and theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough woollen cloth from Scotland, and suits made from it, are known by this name.

clue.text: Home Counties girl is content

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, abbreviated SE
Rene is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from near London is happy with life.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and untroubled is close to feeling content and at peace.
